map_role: Portrait recomposition of Nadirspan: asymmetrically wall-anchored hanging foundry in a deep descending industrial shaft
macro_topology: A vertical central shaft with seven nonuniform cliff-founded overhangs, alternating opposed industrial rooms and a continuous open return
density_profile: Upper ore intake dense; open shaft interlock; dense furnace and ladle at opposing sides; large sparse rejoin; clustered unequal extrusion drums; enclosed quench; sparse freight exit
strong_motifs: Asymmetric cliff-rooted suspension plates in seven distinct altitude bays
Copper-coupled refractory furnace with enclosed lava
Heavy suspended ladle and independently banked counterweight
Three nonidentical machine rotors with separate grounded anchorage
Refractory-shielded water quench and triangular freight davit
interesting_relationships: Production causal chain rotates in architectural order without rotating any existing source cells
Roof-rooted machinery becomes alternating cliff ceiling loads rather than floor-founded trays
Static 200×130 obstruction forces a longer authentic 31×27 Midge path while retaining all named sites
Heavy functional stages sit above editable undercroft pockets and sidewall service corridors

procedural_exemplar_value: Aspect-transfer rule: convert a long ceiling-hung lateral industrial process into stacked alternating nonidentical roof-rooted cells
Explicit structural load paths for hanging rotors and sealed reactive hazards
Reusable cross-shaft branch/rejoin graph and proven whole-hull obstacle recovery
Editable dry negative spaces that do not invalidate route continuity
similarity_avoidance: Unlike source Nadirspan's full-width continuous roof and low horizontal return, this uses interrupted wall-to-ceiling load paths and a descending two-sided process. Unlike Quoin faultwell, these vertical ledges carry identifiable foundry machinery and interleaved worker areas rather than geological survey stations. Unlike Axlewell freight-hoist, production rather than cargo classification dominates.

aspect_transfer.creator: B
preserved: Ceiling-/overhang-rooted loads supporting every major machine with actual structural material
Ore handling, a sealed hot furnace, suspended ladle, three unequal extrusion rotors, enclosed quench and freight davit
Maintenance/repair below heavy machinery, substantial deliberately vacant dry space
Two flight lanes with a blocking-obstruction detour and accessible recovery points
transformed: One nearly horizontal continuous overhead source roof becomes seven unequal and alternating cliff-anchored ceiling overhangs down a deep shaft
Source west-to-east furnace→ladle→caster→quench→freight causality becomes upper-to-lower cross-shaft process adjacency
Long low-altitude source return becomes a pair of alternately entered sidewall recovery galleries alongside the central descent
Exposed extrusion wheels are staged in an asymmetrical vertical cascade with individual engineering load paths
discarded: Source original 2048-wide continuous shallow roof silhouette
Original exact geometry, coordinates, material placement and source shortest-flight path
East rim extraction location and broad continuous undercroft
newly_introduced: Tall open central cargo shaft with unequal side-wall mechanical staging
Three different rotor arrangements separated across two elevations
Sealed mid-depth quench receiver and descending dispatch davit
Entered upper and lower interlocks suitable for a real material obstruction experiment
aspect_transfer.preservation_scale: Native 1:1 Midge material-cell scale, 1024×2048; no rotation, crop, stretch, coordinate reuse or image transplant
